newsitem.title: USA: Georgia state Senate passes welfare bill.
newsitem.headline: Georgia state Senate passes welfare bill.

text.p: The Georgia Senate overwhelmingly passed Gov. Zell Miller's welfare proposal, which caps benefits at four years, or one year sooner than the federal government requires, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution said Friday.
The proposal, approved 54-1, still must be approved by the House.
It would provide assistance to legal immigrants for only one year, and give tax credits to employers who hire welfare recipients.

The proposal prohibit families from getting assistance for children born more than 10 months after they began receiving welfare benefits, unless the birth results from rape or incest, and mandates family planning.
It also requires unwed mothers receiving benefits to cooperate with state efforts to identify and collect support from their childrens' fathers.
